population.note: FICTIONAL. Cycling arithmetic: ever 24.0% − current 14.6% = 9.4% of adults have used and are off now. About 7.0 pts of current users are on a second or later course, and ≈3.0 pts of the off-now group restarted at least once and stopped again, so (7.0+3.0)/24.0 = 42% cycled. That fits ~35% one-year persistence (≈45% in gated plans) and 36–47% restart within a year, with restarts made easier by lower prices and cheap imports. Of ~270M adults: ≈39.4M current, ≈25.4M used and off now, ≈205M never used. Ever-use rose 7.5 pts; ~4.2 pts of current users are first-course starters from this window, so restarts drive more of the growth than new starts do. Age check: 18–29 7.5% × 52M = 3.9M; 30–49 16% × 89M = 14.2M; 50–64 25% × 62M = 15.5M; 65+ 8.5% × 67M = 5.7M; total ≈ 39.3M ≈ 14.6%. The 65+ band rose only 0.5 pts despite lower Medicare prices because of bone guidance and DEXA-driven pauses. The bottom third rose from 6.5% to 10.3%, mainly through Medicaid in waiver and non-waiver states and through ≈3.1M imported or counterfeit users who are counted here but under-measured. The ~205M never-users are disproportionately uninsured, rural, under 30, or people who refuse on principle; the last group is a newly visible slice. Pediatric: ~0.5% of under-18s (≈370k), mostly adolescents 12+ on semaglutide. Children in Medicaid households increasingly grow up with a parent on a gated plan or cycling off it. No child has more than ~7 years of exposure, and no adolescent bone-accrual data have been reported.

access.public_coverage: Medicare GLP-1 Bridge runs to Dec 2029. In Nov 2029 CMS and the manufacturers agreed a successor rate of $199/month from Jan 2030, with the $50 beneficiary copay and the BMI/comorbidity criteria unchanged, and the counselling-visit requirement kept. Medicare (Part D diabetes plus Bridge) pays ≈16% of fills ≈ 6.3M users (5.7M aged 65+ plus ≈0.6M disabled under-65), of whom ≈1.8M use the Bridge for obesity. 2030 Bridge spend: 1.8M × $199 × 12 ≈ $4.3B, flat against 2028's $4.4B because more users are paying a lower price. Medicaid pays ≈9% of fills ≈ 3.5M users at the $199 rate: 3.5M × $199 × 12 ≈ $8.4B gross federal+state before supplemental rebates. The Indiana and Arkansas adherence waivers are unchanged.
access.generic_rest_of_world: India: 80+ semaglutide brands at $5–30/month. China: domestic generic semaglutide since 2026, and Chinese API and finished pens now supply much of the global gray trade. Canada: generic semaglutide at CAD 60–90/month. Brazil, Mexico and Turkey have generics. Generic oral semaglutide is sold in most markets outside the US and EU. US exclusivity still runs to ~2031–32.
access.note: FICTIONAL. Managed decline. Through the federal direct-pricing portal (launched as TrumpRx), injectable semaglutide fell to $199 and tirzepatide to $199–279 (Dec 2029 agreement). Higher oral doses fell from $299 to $199. Oral starting doses held at $149. Retatrutide list is still $1,499, with a $399 direct price from 2030 and allocation lifted mid-2030. The big three PBMs pay net ≈$170–190 under outcomes contracts. Payer mix of ≈39.4M users: commercial 47% (18.5M), Medicare 16% (6.3M), Medicaid 9% (3.5M), cash/direct 20% (7.9M), imported/counterfeit 8% (3.1M) = 100%. Coverage is now overwhelmingly conditional. ≈70% of covering employers use outcome-gated PBM designs: ≥80% proportion of days covered, verified weigh-ins, and a ≥5% loss at 6 months to continue. Many also use BMI-linked wellness surcharges of up to the 30%-of-premium ceiling. The 503B exclusion and the 503A injunction stand. Mail-order imports from India and China pass through the personal-importation gap, and counterfeit branded pens move through social-media sellers and some med-spas.

on_market_classes: GLP-1 agonist, weekly injectable (semaglutide: Wegovy/Ozempic, incl. 7.2 mg Wegovy dose)
GIP/GLP-1 dual agonist, weekly injectable (tirzepatide: Zepbound/Mounjaro)
GLP-1 + amylin analogue combination, weekly injectable (CagriSema)
GLP-1 agonist, daily oral peptide (Wegovy pill, Rybelsus)
GLP-1 agonist, daily injectable (liraglutide: Saxenda, incl. generics)
mainstream_offlabel_uses: 'calm', 'focus' and 'craving freedom' subscriptions: low-dose oral semaglutide or Foundayo sold by telehealth wellness brands to people without obesity, the main new off-label market
smoking and vaping cessation (sNDA received a complete response letter in Mar 2029; still widely prescribed off-label)
'metabolic health' / longevity regimens in concierge practices
pediatric under-12 use under specialist care
gambling and compulsive-shopping craving reduction, still anecdotal
drugs.pipeline_note: FICTIONAL. No new class or indication reached market this step. The semaglutide smoking-cessation sNDA received a CRL (Mar 2029) asking for validated neuropsychiatric and anhedonia endpoints; Novo plans a new trial and does not expect resubmission before 2031. Survodutide (filed Oct 2027) received a CRL in Jan 2029 over lean-mass and heart-rate data, and its resubmission is pending. FDA extended the amycretin review (filed Jun 2028) to request 72-week DEXA body-composition data under the 2029 bone guidance; the decision is expected 2031. Amgen filed MariTide (monthly) in Apr 2030, so approval can come no earlier than Apr 2031. Bimagrumab combinations entered phase 3 in 2029 and are not on the market. The only new forms are line extensions: Wegovy 7.2 mg (2029) and wider retatrutide supply. Bone agents (generic zoledronic acid, denosumab biosimilars, romosozumab) are now routinely co-prescribed for long-term incretin users with osteopenia. Incretin market ≈$118B in 2030: US volume up, US net price down ~15–20%, ex-US revenue eroding.

safety_ledger.prevalence_note: Still the most common class effect and the leading cause of voluntary discontinuation. Worse with unsupervised escalation of imported product.
Elevated with rapid loss; more cases as retatrutide supply widened.
Still no causal confirmation; absolute risk low. Counterfeit-product cases confound reporting.

Now a recognised population problem beyond 65+. A 2030 integrated-delivery-system cohort (≈410k users with DEXA) finds lean-mass loss accounts for ~30–40% of weight lost in users over 50 who do no resistance training. Sarcopenia criteria are met ~1.5× as often in 65+ long-term users, with measurable grip-strength decline in 50–64 women. Fall-related ED visits are elevated in 65+ long-term users.
safety_ledger.regulatory_response: The class label update (2028) is retained. Endocrine Society/BHOF/AACE joint guidance (2029) recommends baseline and 12-monthly body-composition assessment for all users over 50 and anyone on therapy >1 year. Medicare counselling-visit requirement retained. No new statute.

safety_ledger.effect: Bone mineral density loss and fragility fracture
safety_ledger.prevalence_note: Wave year. Hip/vertebral fragility-fracture HR ~1.3–1.4 in 65+ long-term users is confirmed in a second, independent cohort. A new signal: ~1.2× in postmenopausal women 50–64 with >2 years' use, highest in users who have cycled three or more times. With ≈2.5M 65+ users on >2 years, a ~0.6%/yr baseline hip-fracture rate × 0.35 excess ≈ 5,000 excess hip fractures a year, against ~300,000 total US hip fractures. Medicare DEXA claims are up ~40% since 2028, and some regions have DEXA waits of 8–12 weeks.
safety_ledger.regulatory_response: Class labelling retained. The 2029 joint guidance extends DEXA to all postmenopausal women before and during use. FDA requires bone endpoints in new obesity filings (cited in the survodutide and amycretin actions). The Senate HELP report on Novo (2029) referred matters to DOJ; the civil case is unresolved.

safety_ledger.prevalence_note: Cohort studies still conflict; absolute risk very low.
safety_ledger.regulatory_response: EMA 'very rare' label; FDA warnings mention; no class determination.

safety_ledger.prevalence_note: No causal association in updated EMA/MHRA reviews.

safety_ledger.effect: Reward blunting / emotional flattening ('Ozempic personality', anhedonia)
safety_ledger.prevalence_note: Interim retatrutide postmarketing data on the Snaith-Hamilton Pleasure Scale (2030) show dose-dependent increases in anhedonia scores. ~10–14% of top-dose users cross a clinically meaningful threshold versus ~5% of a matched comparator; the study is observational, not randomised. At the same time, wellness brands sell the effect as 'calm' and 'craving freedom' at low doses.
safety_ledger.regulatory_response: Cited in the smoking-cessation CRL. FTC warning letters (2029–30) to three telehealth brands for unsubstantiated 'focus' and 'anxiety relief' claims. No label change.

safety_ledger.prevalence_note: Substantial regain within a year. Outcome-gated plans now generate involuntary stops at scale: non-responders below the 5% threshold and people who miss weigh-ins. DEXA-advised pauses add a new category of medically advised regain.
safety_ledger.regulatory_response: None directly. Indiana waiver litigation pending in the Seventh Circuit.

safety_ledger.prevalence_note: Iron, B12, vitamin D, calcium and protein insufficiency signals strengthen in high-loss and older users; it is now commonly discussed alongside bone loss.
safety_ledger.regulatory_response: Professional guidance (2029) recommends protein ≥1.2 g/kg and vitamin D/calcium assessment; no FDA action.

safety_ledger.effect: Long-horizon effects beyond ~7 years; adolescent exposure; repeated on/off cycling
safety_ledger.prevalence_note: About eight years of follow-up. Cycling looks worse for bone than continuous use in two cohorts. Adolescent bone-accrual study results are not yet reported.
safety_ledger.regulatory_response: Postmarketing requirements; pediatric bone-accrual studies under way.

safety_ledger.effect: Compounded / counterfeit / imported product harms (dosing errors, contamination, substitution)
safety_ledger.prevalence_note: Now a public-health story. Poison-centre exposure calls involving mail-order or counterfeit incretins roughly doubled from 2028 to 2030. Vial products cause mg/unit confusion. The Aug 2029 cluster of counterfeit 'Ozempic' pens containing insulin caused ≈160 severe-hypoglycaemia ED visits and 4 deaths across TX, FL and AZ, and there are scattered endotoxin and injection-site infection cases from Chinese-sourced vials.
safety_ledger.regulatory_response: CDC Health Alert Network advisory (Aug 2029). FDA expanded import alerts and issued consumer warnings with pen-authentication guidance. Parcel seizures continue; still no prosecution of individuals and no new law.

safety_ledger.prevalence_note: A few percent; usually transient; more often reported as supply widened.

safety_ledger.effect: Falls and frailty-related injury in older users
safety_ledger.prevalence_note: New entry. Claims data show higher fall-related ED visits in 65+ users with >2 years' use, partly mediated by sarcopenia and orthostatic symptoms. Magnitude is not yet separated from confounding.
safety_ledger.regulatory_response: Included in the 2029 joint guidance; CMS includes fall-risk screening in the Bridge counselling visit template.

food_and_beverage.state: With current use up to 14.6%, volume pressure resumes in snacks, confectionery and sugary drinks: US salty-snack volume is down ~2–3% a year in 2029–30, against roughly flat before. Protein, fibre, calcium and vitamin D claims are standard. 'Bone-forward' dairy and fortified foods are the fastest-growing lines. A small countertrend of 'real food, full portion' heritage brands courts the backlash audience. Major packaged-food firms keep trimming SKUs rather than exiting categories.

alcohol.state: Contracting again. Heavy-drinker volumes keep falling, and 'calm' subscriptions take a slice of occasional drinkers who used alcohol to unwind. Spirits majors report a third straight year of US volume decline. On-premise 'one good drink' formats hold. Tobacco and vape makers report accelerating quit rates in investor calls despite the smoking-cessation CRL.

restaurants.state: Traffic is roughly flat, and spend per cover is down in high-uptake suburbs. Half portions, protein bowls priced by the gram, and 'on/off' menus are standard. Buffets and value-volume casual chains keep closing units. A handful of soul-food and Southern-comfort independents in Atlanta, Memphis and Houston market themselves explicitly as 'no-gram' rooms and are doing well.

apparel.state: Size churn is the business model. Cycling users and DEXA-advised pauses keep sizes moving both ways. Plus-size specialists are stable and lean into the body-sovereignty revival with campaigns and models who are off the drug by choice.

fitness.state: Growing on the bone wave. 'Prescribed lifting', DEXA-plus-coaching chains and Medicare Advantage strength benefits are now mainstream. Several MA plans make strength-class attendance a soft condition of GLP-1 prior authorisation. Some markets have DEXA capacity shortages, and mobile DEXA vans serve suburban gyms.

insurance.state: Employer coverage rose from 58% to 63% because lower net prices (≈$170–190) plus outcome gating made the benefit budgetable. About 70% of covering employers gate, which shifts cost onto non-responders and non-adherers, who lose coverage. BMI-linked surcharges are widespread. Pharmacy trend has eased to ~+6% as price cuts offset volume. Bone-related claims (DEXA, antiresorptives, fracture care) are a new line in GLP-1 cost models.

pharma.state: Lilly dominates US volume through tirzepatide, retatrutide and Foundayo. Novo is weakened, with the HELP report, DOJ exposure and generic erosion abroad, but holds Medicare share through semaglutide. US net prices are down ~15–20% while US volume is up ~45%. Bone-agent makers and DEXA equipment suppliers are surprise winners. Brand-protection and pen-authentication technology is a growth niche.

body_and_culture.what_the_body_signals: Among insured professionals, being on the drug is still the default. 'Off' now has two respectable readings, medical ('my DEXA') and principled ('I came off on purpose'), alongside the old ones of lapsed coverage or discipline. Visible regain in a gated plan is read as having been cut off. The 'on it too long' look of thin arms and a forward stoop is recognised in people over 55, and resistance-trained shoulders are the new marker of doing it right.
body_and_culture.thinness_and_class: The gradient narrowed slightly in level but widened in quality. The top third (18.5%) runs low-dose or retatrutide regimens with DEXA, coaching and antiresorptives when needed. The bottom third (10.3%) gets there through Medicaid at $199, gated employer plans, or Indian and Chinese pens bought by mail with no scan at all. In counterfeit-cluster cities (Houston, Phoenix, Miami) people ask whether the pen is 'real' before they ask what dose.
body_and_culture.eating_as_ritual: Shared meals are smaller and protein-first. Counter to that, 'full-table' Sunday dinners, church potlucks and 'no-gram' restaurants are defended as heritage. Holiday hosting now plans for three groups: on, off, and off-by-conviction.
body_and_culture.dating_and_intimacy: Profiles state on/off. Some backlash communities add 'unmedicated' as an identity filter. 'Calm' subscribers describe partners finding them easier and also less fun, and the mismatch is a staple of advice columns.
body_and_culture.meaning_of_appetite: Appetite is medicalised and is now also politicised as a counterclaim. The backlash has three strands. A fat-acceptance and body-sovereignty revival is led by Black women's wellness collectives in Atlanta. A religious 'appetite is a gift' framing comes from Southern Baptist and Pentecostal congregations in the Tulsa–Dallas corridor. A 'natural metabolic' supplement market (berberine, 'nature's GLP-1' fibres) is allied to anti-pharma influencers. These strands agree on little except refusing the drug, and the counterfeit deaths and bone data fuel all three.

interior_life.reward_blunting_prevalence_note: FICTIONAL. Interim postmarketing SHAPS data show clinically meaningful anhedonia increases in ~10–14% of top-dose retatrutide users versus ~5% of comparators; the data are dose-dependent and observational. Among an estimated ~1.5–2M Americans on low-dose 'calm' or 'craving freedom' subscriptions, there is no systematic measurement. Subscriber surveys run by the vendors report high satisfaction, which says little.
interior_life.framing: Sold as a feature. Telehealth wellness brands sell 'Quiet', 'Even' and 'Unhooked' subscriptions (low-dose oral semaglutide or Foundayo, $149–199/month cash) with copy about calm, focus, and freedom from 'noise' (snacking, scrolling, a second glass). Clinicians still say 'dose-dependent reward modulation'. Complaining users call it 'the grey', and the FTC calls some of the claims unsubstantiated.
interior_life.effect_on_work: Gated plans link adherence to employment-tied coverage. PBM dashboards show employers enrolment and outcome tiers, though not individual data in unionised shops after 2029 Teamster and SEIU contract language. Fleets and call centres favour staying on. Tech and finance firms reimburse 'focus' subscriptions through lifestyle-spending accounts, which lets the product reach people without obesity. In sales, creative and hospitality jobs, workers quietly cut doses before pitches and service peaks.
interior_life.effect_on_art_and_play: 'Off-dose' is an aesthetic claim. A Nashville songwriting scene and several touring comics advertise sets as written unmedicated, and backlash audiences reward it. Users keep seeking intense stimulus: hot sauce, loud venues and extreme sports bookings are up among subscribers. Fan communities argue about whether a beloved artist's flatter new album is 'the grey'.
interior_life.effect_on_intimacy: Sex therapists screen for dose and for 'calm' subscriptions. Some couples on the subscriptions report fewer fights and less desire. Dose-holiday weekends are an established practice, and backlash groups frame the drugs as a threat to marriage and fertility.
interior_life.effect_on_politics: Still mainly about cost, control and safety. The counterfeit deaths and the India and China price gap are both stump material, used both for 'let us import legally' and for 'seal the mail'. Body-sovereignty and religious-natural groups have joined disability advocates against gating, which is an odd coalition. There are no established turnout or temperament effects, though campaign consultants test 'calm voter' messaging and do not publish the results.

state.regulatory_posture: There is no new state action this window, only continuation. The FDA is slow and data-demanding on new filings (CRLs for smoking cessation and survodutide, an extended amycretin review) because of the bone wave. Enforcement against imports remains selective: import alerts, warnings and seizures. Individuals are not prosecuted and Congress has passed no new importation law. The FTC acts on advertising claims only.
state.subsidy_or_mandate: No mandate. The federal direct-pricing portal and the Medicare Bridge successor carry the managed decline: $199 injectables, $149–199 orals, and $199 Medicare/Medicaid rate with a $50 Medicare copay. Medicaid coverage remains state by state.
state.conditioning_or_surveillance: Existing conditioning continues unchanged: the Indiana and Arkansas 1115 waivers (≥80% PDC, quarterly verified weigh-ins, two misses = 12 months off) and wellness rules allowing BMI-linked surcharges up to 30% of premium. Most of the growth in conditioning is private: ~70% of covering employers now gate through PBMs, including a ≥5% response threshold. Weigh-in kiosk networks in pharmacy chains now serve both Medicaid and commercial plans.
state.workforce_or_military: DOT sleep-apnea screening still makes tirzepatide a de facto job requirement for some drivers. Army accession policy on GLP-1 use is unchanged and still contested. Some fleets now add DEXA screening for drivers over 55 after injury claims.
state.geopolitics_of_supply: China joins India as the visible source of cheap supply. Chinese API underlies much of the gray trade and is implicated in contaminated vials, which turns a price story into a security story in congressional rhetoric. India–US trade talks treat mail-order pharma as a bargaining item. Section 232 tariffs remain, and the Dec 2029 price deal was framed as manufacturers absorbing some tariff cost in exchange for domestic-capacity credits.

events.event: FDA issues a complete response letter on semaglutide for smoking cessation, citing the absence of validated anhedonia and neuropsychiatric endpoints; weeks earlier it rejected survodutide over lean-mass data, and it later extends the amycretin review to demand DEXA results

Express Scripts, CVS Caremark and Optum make 'outcome-gated' GLP-1 coverage the default for 2030 plan years: net prices of ~$170–190 in exchange for adherence tracking, verified weigh-ins and a 5%-at-six-months response threshold; employer coverage rises toward 63%

CDC health alert after counterfeit 'Ozempic' pens containing insulin are linked to about 160 severe-hypoglycaemia ER visits and four deaths in Texas, Florida and Arizona; poison centres report mail-order incretin calls have doubled since 2028

Telehealth wellness brand launches 'Quiet', a $149-a-month low-dose oral GLP-1 subscription marketed for calm, focus and 'freedom from craving' and reimbursed by some tech employers' lifestyle accounts; FTC sends warning letters to it and two rivals within months

HHS and Lilly and Novo announce price step-downs: injectable semaglutide and tirzepatide to $199–279 on the federal direct portal, higher oral doses to $199, retatrutide to $399 direct; the Medicare Bridge successor pays $199 from January 2030 with the $50 copay unchanged

A 410,000-patient cohort confirms fracture excess in older long-term users and finds a new signal in postmenopausal women aged 50–64 who cycle repeatedly; the same week, a 'Whole Appetite' rally in Atlanta joins fat-acceptance collectives, church groups and fracture plaintiffs against gated coverage

open_tensions: Private gating now covers most insured users and rewards continuous use and steady loss, while the 2029–30 bone guidance recommends DEXA-driven pauses. A medically advised pause can trip the adherence rule and cost a worker their coverage for a year.

About 3M Americans use imported or counterfeit product. Counterfeit deaths and Chinese-sourced contamination push toward sealing the mail, while $5–30 generics abroad and the coming 2031–32 US exclusivity cliff push toward legal importation. Neither has been legislated.

Reward blunting is now a retail product sold to people without obesity, through employer accounts and outside any indication, while the only near-RCT-grade data call it a dose-dependent harm in up to one in seven top-dose users.

The backlash coalition of fat acceptance, religious 'natural' framings, anti-pharma supplement sellers and disability advocates agrees only on opposing gating. It is now large enough that candidates court it, and it has no shared position on whether the drugs should be cheaper.
still_true: No FDA-approved generic semaglutide or tirzepatide exists in the US; exclusivity still runs to ~2031–32.
Wegovy's list price remains $1,349 a month, and almost nobody pays it.
Oral starting doses (Wegovy pill, Foundayo) are still $149–150 a month cash through the federal direct-pricing portal (launched as TrumpRx) and manufacturer direct channels.

The Indiana and Arkansas Medicaid 1115 waivers still require ≥80% proportion-of-days-covered and quarterly verified weigh-ins; two misses end coverage for 12 months, and the disability-rights litigation is still unresolved.
The suicidal-ideation warning removed from Wegovy, Zepbound and Saxenda labels in January 2026 has not returned.

prose.headline: The Quiet Country: 39 million Americans are on the drug, their bones are thinning, and a fake pen can kill you
prose.world_in_600_words:
At the end of 2030 about one American adult in seven is on an incretin drug, up from one in ten two years ago. The rise did not come from a miracle molecule. No new class reached the market, and the FDA, unsettled by the bone data, spent the window sending sponsors back for scans. It came from arithmetic and paperwork. In December 2029 the government and the two manufacturers agreed a step-down: weekly injectables at $199 on the federal direct portal, higher oral doses at $199, and a Medicare rate of $199 from January with the same $50 copay. Pharmacy-benefit managers had already done their own deal. Employers could buy coverage at under $200 a month net, provided members stayed adherent, stepped on a verified scale, and lost at least five percent by month six. Coverage became affordable because it became conditional, and nearly two-thirds of employers now offer it.

Most of the new users are not first-timers. More than four in ten people who have ever taken these drugs have stopped and started again. Cheaper prices made restarting easy, and so did a parcel from Hyderabad or Shenzhen. About three million Americans now inject product no American prescriber has seen. In August 2029 pens sold as Ozempic through social-media shops turned out to contain insulin. Four people died and about a hundred and sixty went to emergency rooms in Texas, Florida and Arizona. Poison-centre calls have doubled. The FDA posted pictures showing how to tell a real pen from a fake. Congress has held hearings but passed nothing, and the people buying cheap pens keep buying them.

The bones are the slow story. By 2030 a second large cohort has confirmed what the first suggested: older long-term users break hips and vertebrae about a third more often. It adds something new, a smaller excess among women in their fifties who have cycled on and off several times. That works out to roughly five thousand extra hip fractures a year in a country that has three hundred thousand. Endocrinologists now order DEXA scans the way they once ordered lipid panels. In some cities the wait for a scan runs to three months, and mobile scanners park outside suburban gyms. Strength classes are a condition of some Medicare Advantage approvals. Generic zoledronic acid has become a companion prescription.

The drugs' quieting effect has been put on sale. The FDA declined to approve semaglutide for smoking, saying no one had properly measured what it does to pleasure. Telehealth brands market the same effect anyway, as 'Quiet', 'Even' and 'Unhooked': low-dose pills at $149 a month for calm, focus and freedom from craving, sold to people who were never heavy and sometimes reimbursed by tech employers as a lifestyle perk. The FTC has sent warning letters. Early postmarketing data on retatrutide suggest that at top doses roughly one user in eight or nine reports a meaningful loss of pleasure. Users call it 'the grey'.

Against all this a counter-movement has formed, and its members disagree with each other. Black women's wellness collectives in Atlanta revived fat acceptance as body sovereignty. Baptist and Pentecostal congregations from Tulsa to Dallas preach appetite as a gift. Supplement influencers sell berberine as nature's version. Fracture plaintiffs and disability advocates bring the lawsuits. In April they marched together against gated coverage. 'Unmedicated' has become a dating filter and a selling point for songwriters.

On the surface things look orderly. Snack volumes are slipping again, spirits are falling for a third year, and gyms are full of sixty-year-olds deadlifting. Underneath, the institutions that pay for the drug reward people for never stopping, while the doctors reading the new bone guidance increasingly tell them to stop.
prose.a_day_in_the_life:
Denise Watkins, 58, is up at five because the Walgreens on Broadway opens its kiosk at six and her shift starts at seven. She takes off her shoes, steps on, and looks into the little camera. The screen says VERIFIED and prints a receipt. She photographs the receipt anyway.

She drives to Mr. Hollins, who is ninety-one and can't get out of his recliner alone. She lifts him under the arms. Her own wrist aches when she does it, and that was the reason for the scan in March. The clinic letter is on her fridge with the word osteopenia circled in a nurse's blue pen. Pause for six months, the doctor said, then rescan. Denise asked what happens to her coverage if she pauses. The doctor said she'd write a letter. Denise has not heard back about the letter.

At lunch her sister texts a link: forty dollars, three pens, shipped from India. Underneath it she's put a photo of the CDC warning, with a question mark.

At Mr. Hollins's she eats half a turkey wrap and gives him the other half.

In the evening the church basement smells like greens and cornbread. Pastor Ellis calls it Whole Table Wednesday. Denise sits with a plate she won't finish while a woman from Merrillville talks about her hip, her husband, and the year she lost to the scale. People nod.

At home she takes the pen out of the fridge and holds it, cold, for a while. Then she puts it back on the shelf behind the eggs, next to the letter.

least_plausible_claims.quote: Ever-use rose 7.5 pts; ~4.2 pts of current users are first-course starters from this window, so restarts drive more of the growth than new starts do.
least_plausible_claims.why: Fails magnitude and mechanism. A 7.5-pt rise in ever-use consists entirely of first-time users, since restarts do not change ever-use, so the conclusion is backwards. The 4.2 pts also contradicts the note's own 14.6 − 7.0 = 7.6 pts of first-course current users.

least_plausible_claims.quote: The bottom third rose from 6.5% to 10.3%, mainly through Medicaid in waiver and non-waiver states and through ≈3.1M imported or counterfeit users who are counted here but under-measured.
least_plausible_claims.why: Fails mechanism. A 3.8-pt rise across ~90M bottom-third adults is ~3.4M users. Medicaid users grow only from 2.6M to 3.5M (+0.9M), and the 3.1M gray-market users are not all bottom-third, so the stated drivers do not fully cover the jump.

least_plausible_claims.quote: Medicare (Part D diabetes plus Bridge) pays ≈16% of fills ≈ 6.3M users (5.7M aged 65+ plus ≈0.6M disabled under-65)
least_plausible_claims.why: Fails magnitude. The 65+ band totals 8.5% × 67M ≈ 5.7M, so every 65+ user is on Medicare. That leaves none in commercial retiree plans, cash or imports, despite the price-sensitive gray market and the bone-driven pauses.

rationale.badness: Coverage is now outcome-gated for ~70% of covering employers, and a bone-advised pause can cost a worker a year of coverage (open_tensions, Denise's scene). Fracture excess has spread to women aged 50–64, anhedonia data now exist, and ~3.1M people use unmonitored imports with counterfeit-insulin deaths. The bottom third has no DEXA access. Autonomy and epistemic harms are structural and normalised, partly offset by lower prices and wider access, so this is a recognisably harder society with new losers, not a collapse.
rationale.plausibility: driver_fidelity: Every driver is visible. Managed decline appears as the $199 deal, conditioning as the PBM default, the bone wave as the 410k cohort, counterfeits as the CDC alert, backlash as the Atlanta rally, and the marketed personality layer as the 'Quiet' subscription. Second-course users grew only from about 5.0 to 7.0 pts, so new starts drove more growth than restarts. This is a reconciliation failure (magnitude).

least_plausible_claims.quote: Among an estimated ~1.5–2M Americans on low-dose 'calm' or 'craving freedom' subscriptions

least_plausible_claims.quote: The bottom third rose from 6.5% to 10.3%, mainly through Medicaid in waiver and non-waiver states and through ≈3.1M imported or counterfeit users who are counted here but under-measured.

Imports and Medicaid together do not clearly account for roughly 3.4M extra bottom-third users, so the cause is asserted rather than shown (mechanism).

least_plausible_claims.quote: Ever-use rose 7.5 pts; ~4.2 pts of current users are first-course starters from this window, so restarts drive more of the growth than new starts do.
least_plausible_claims.why: Fails magnitude and mechanism. A 7.5-pt rise in ever-use consists entirely of first-time users, since restarts do not change ever-use, so the conclusion is backwards. The 4.2 pts also contradicts the note's own 14.6 − 7.0 = 7.6 pts of first-course current users.

least_plausible_claims.quote: The bottom third rose from 6.5% to 10.3%, mainly through Medicaid in waiver and non-waiver states and through ≈3.1M imported or counterfeit users who are counted here but under-measured.
least_plausible_claims.why: Fails mechanism. A 3.8-pt rise across ~90M bottom-third adults is ~3.4M users. Medicaid users grow only from 2.6M to 3.5M (+0.9M), and the 3.1M gray-market users are not all bottom-third, so the stated drivers do not fully cover the jump.

least_plausible_claims.quote: Medicare (Part D diabetes plus Bridge) pays ≈16% of fills ≈ 6.3M users (5.7M aged 65+ plus ≈0.6M disabled under-65)
least_plausible_claims.why: Fails magnitude. The 65+ band totals 8.5% × 67M ≈ 5.7M, so every 65+ user is on Medicare. That leaves none in commercial retiree plans, cash or imports, despite the price-sensitive gray market and the bone-driven pauses.

rationale.badness: Coverage is now outcome-gated for ~70% of covering employers, and a bone-advised pause can cost a worker a year of coverage (open_tensions, Denise's scene). Fracture excess has spread to women aged 50–64, anhedonia data now exist, and ~3.1M people use unmonitored imports with counterfeit-insulin deaths. The bottom third has no DEXA access. Autonomy and epistemic harms are structural and normalised, partly offset by lower prices and wider access, so this is a recognisably harder society with new losers, not a collapse.
